title: 2022 HMMT February Team Problem 5
statement: Let \(A B C\) be a triangle with centroid \(G\), and let \(E\) and \(F\) be points on side \(B C\) such that \(B E=E F=F C\). Points \(X\) and \(Y\) lie on lines \(A B\) and \(A C\), respectively, so that \(X, Y\), and \(G\) are not collinear. If the line through \(E\) parallel to \(X G\) and the line through \(F\) parallel to \(Y G\) intersect at \(P \neq G\), prove that \(G P\) passes through the midpoint of \(X Y\).

solutions.text: Solution: Let \(C G\) intersect \(A B\) at \(N\). Then \(N\) is the midpoint of \(A B\) and it is known that \(\frac{C G}{A B}=2=\) \(\frac{C E}{E B}\), so \(E G \| A B\). Moreover, since \(F E=E B\), we have \([E F G]=[E X G]\). Similarly, \([E F G]=[F Y G]\). Now we have \([P X G]=[E X G]=[E F G]=[F Y G]=[P Y G]\), so \(P G\) bisects \(X Y\), as desired.
